record.author: アオキ

source: Research/App Store Reviews/33. Habitify - Habit Tracker - Daily Goals, Routine & Streaks/reviews.jsonl

record.title: Widget Update Ruined the Tracking Flexibility
record.body: I used to love the old iOS home screen widget, where I could increment my habit progress one step at a time. For example, if I had to complete a habit twice a day, I could mark it once in the morning and once again later. Now, with the new widget, a single tap completes the entire habit, making it impossible to track partial progress throughout the day. This removes the flexibility and satisfaction of tracking habits gradually. Please bring back the old widget behavior or at least add an option to choose how the widget marks progress.
record.author: RogerArt99

source: Research/App Store Reviews/52. ShineDay - Habit Tracker - Micro Habits, ADHD & Focus/reviews.jsonl

record.title: Fantastic App
record.body: I likely have ADHD and I really struggle with staying on task. Some people might be able to think of ‘get ready’ as one task but for me I have no idea which thing to do first. I get distracted easily and have 4 little ones so it’s always manic in the mornings. With this app I can have all the individual tasks I need to do on my widget screen, tap the one I’ve done and it disappears. It makes me feel so much more organised and on track. I love that I can name each task, choose an icon to represent it, change its colour and assign it to a specific section of the day. I have begun using Todoist for chores and general tasks that need doing but Tiny Routines is amazing for the specific steps of daily routines. Highly recommend!
record.author: Juiice

source: Research/App Store Reviews/53. HabitMinder • Habit Tracker - Daily Reminders & Routines/reviews.jsonl

record.title: Outstanding - almost there
record.body:
Habit apps are a crowded marketplace, and this one really stands out to me. Gorgeous design that is very simple and easy on the eyes, but still very flexible. They found the right balance. It’s engaging and fun to check things off (might as well use the addictiveness of technology to help your productivity :) Their hydration app is equally fantastic. Both have earned a permanent spot in my “Today” view...assuming a few things are in the works. 

1. Mac app - visibility and management of tasks/habits is really only viable if you can access them (and synced notifications) from any device. 

2. The notification text is a bit odd. I wish these would just contain the habit text and nothing else. They often appear as verbose sentences that you have to read. For me this affects the fluidity of use. 

3. The Today widget could be enhanced by only showing remaining habits at the top. 

4. Ability both to skip habits or mark as failed would be nice. 

Items 2–4 are all ways of helping you see only what you need to see. The “at a glance” nature of this app isn’t quite there yet. 

The comments seem to indicate that more integration with multiple devices is forthcoming. Lack of this functionality is normally a dealbreaker for me, but I’m using this on my phone only for the moment because the app is just that good. At whatever point these become more integrated in the ecosystem, this and WaterMinder will unquestionably be 5 star software.

record.author: rheagoel96

source: Research/App Store Reviews/56. Dots - Habit Tracker Widget - Daily Routine, Goal & Planner/reviews.jsonl

record.title: Exceptional, no nonsense app
record.body:
Sensational organisation app. The minimalism is absolutely perfect for people who actually want to track their habits without the faff. My ADHD makes organisation challenging and over the year I’ve tried countless apps that claim to help “neurodivergent people” or be “perfect for those who procrastinate.” They end up being made for quick cash grabs or having a wildly confusing interface that is overwhelming and challenging to navigate. 

With Dots, you get exactly what you download. All your habits trackable in a range of formats (card, list, calendar form) so you can check them off in the one you prefer. You can also add the widget to your home screen so you can cross habits off during the day without having to open the app. There’s no paywall, no ads, and it’s beautifully minimalistic. Everything I needed I am so thankful that I found this.
